worldcombat.skill.stunspore.summary: Toss a puff of numbing powder to where the target stands; it bursts into a cloud that lingers there. Anyone standing in it is kept paralysed, and stepping out lets the paralysis run down its remaining time. It is the only one of the three paralysis moves that stays in the world, so foes can walk around it or wait it out. Grass types pass through powder, Electric types through paralysis.
The puff is thrown to a point within %1$s blocks at %2$s blocks per tick and covers a %3$s block radius on landing.
The cloud lingers for %1$s; non-friendly bodies inside are kept paralysed for %2$s, and leaving still runs that remainder down.
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.thick.on: Thick cloud: radius x0.8, duration x1.3 and paralysis x1.25, but cooldown x1.15 - to seal one patch of ground.
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.thick.off: Loose cloud: radius x1.2, easier to catch several moving targets at once, but shorter, fainter and with a shorter cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.timing: Thrown to a point: range %1$s, windup %2$s, recovery %3$s, costs %4$s PP, cooldown %5$s.
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.growth.1: From level %1$s the cloud radius grows to %2$s blocks.
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.use.1: Make a pursuer slow down in the cloud
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.use.2: Herd enemies into or out of a patch of ground
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.preference.t: On: radius x0.8, duration x1.3 and paralysis x1.25, but cooldown x1.15, to seal one patch of ground. Off: loose cloud, radius x1.2, easier to catch several moving targets at once, but shorter, fainter and with a shorter cooldown.
worldcombat.skill.stunspore.preference.a: Beyond this distance the companion closes in instead of throwing. Larger values chase harder and drop the cloud out of reach more often.
When on, the companion also lays a fresh cloud on a target that is already paralysed, mainly to deny ground with where the cloud sits; when off, it only casts at bodies not yet paralysed.
When on, the companion may leave its post to scatter powder; when off, it only casts at what it can reach from where it stands.
